items.question: My brother ___ sixteen.

explanation.en: 'My brother' is one person (he), so the verb is 'is': My brother is sixteen.
explanation.he: My brother הוא אדם אחד (he), ולכן הפועל הוא is.

items.question: Which sentence is correct?

explanation.en: Use 'an' before a vowel sound (an egg), and don't leave out the verb: It's = It is.
explanation.he: לפני מילה שמתחילה בצליל תנועה משתמשים ב-an: an egg. וגם אי אפשר לוותר על is: It's = It is.

items.question: ___ you a student?

explanation.en: Questions with be start with am, is or are. With 'you' we use 'are': Are you a student? We don't use 'do' with be.
explanation.he: בשאלה עם be הפועל בא בתחילת המשפט. עם you משתמשים ב-are: Are you a student? עם be לא משתמשים ב-do.

items.question: ___ are my shoes.

explanation.en: 'Shoes' is plural, so we need 'these' (or 'those') with 'are'. 'This' and 'that' are for one thing.
explanation.he: shoes היא מילה ברבים, ולכן these (או those). this ו-that משמשים לדבר אחד.

explanation.en: 13 is thirteen. 30 is thirty, 3 is three, and 'third' means number 3 in a list (first, second, third).
explanation.he: thirteen הוא 13. thirty הוא 30, three הוא 3, ו-third פירושו "שלישי" (first, second, third).

prompt.en: It's nine in the morning and you meet a friend. What do you say?
prompt.he: השעה תשע בבוקר ופוגשים חבר. מה אומרים?

items.question: 9:00 in the morning. You meet a friend. You say: ___

explanation.en: When you meet someone in the morning, say 'Good morning'. 'Good night' and 'Goodbye' are for leaving, and 'Good evening' is for the evening.
explanation.he: כשנפגשים בבוקר אומרים Good morning. את Good night ו-Goodbye אומרים כשנפרדים, ואת Good evening אומרים בערב.

items.question: There are seven days in a ___.

explanation.en: A week has seven days. A month has about 30 days, and a year has 12 months.
explanation.he: בשבוע (week) יש שבעה ימים. בחודש (month) יש בערך 30 יום, ובשנה (year) יש 12 חודשים.

items.question: I'm from Israel. I'm ___.

explanation.en: The country is Israel, the nationality is Israeli, and the language is Hebrew.
explanation.he: המדינה: Israel. ישראלי/ת: Israeli. השפה (עברית): Hebrew.

prompt.en: Read the text. How old is Noa?
prompt.he: קראו את הטקסט. בת כמה נועה?

items.question:
Hi! My name is Lior. I'm sixteen, and I'm from Tel Aviv. This is my sister, Noa. She is twenty.

How old is Noa?

explanation.en: The text says 'She is twenty' about Noa. Sixteen (16) is Lior's age.
explanation.he: בטקסט כתוב על נועה: She is twenty, כלומר 20. שש-עשרה (16) הוא הגיל של ליאור.

prompt.en: Read the sign. When is the shop closed?
prompt.he: קראו את השלט. מתי החנות סגורה?

items.question:
Welcome to Tal's Shop! We are open from Sunday to Thursday. We are closed on Friday and Saturday.

When is the shop closed?

explanation.en: The sign says the shop is closed on Friday and Saturday. From Sunday to Thursday it is open.
explanation.he: בשלט כתוב שהחנות סגורה בימי שישי ושבת, ופתוחה מראשון עד חמישי.

items.question: How old is Maya?

explanation.en: Maya says 'seventeen' (17), with the stress at the end: seven-TEEN. 'Seventy' (70) has the stress at the start: SEV-en-ty.
explanation.he: מאיה אומרת seventeen, כלומר 17. ההטעמה בסוף המילה: seven-TEEN. ב-seventy (70) ההטעמה בהתחלה.

prompt.en: Listen. Which day will they meet?

items.audio_text: Bye, Tom! See you on Thursday.
items.question: When will they meet?

explanation.en: 'See you on Thursday' means they will meet on Thursday. Thursday and Tuesday sound similar: Thursday starts with 'th'.
explanation.he: See you on Thursday פירושו "נתראה ביום חמישי". קל להתבלבל בין Thursday (חמישי) ל-Tuesday (שלישי).

items.question: My brother ___ in a bank.

explanation.en: With he, she and it (my brother = he), present simple verbs add -s: he works. 'Is work' mixes two verb forms.
explanation.he: בהווה פשוט, עם he/she/it מוסיפים s לפועל: My brother works. הצורה is work שגויה.

items.question: ___ your parents speak English?

explanation.en: Present simple questions use do or does. 'Your parents' is plural (they), so: Do your parents speak English?
explanation.he: שאלה בהווה פשוט פותחים ב-do או does. your parents הם רבים (they), ולכן Do.

items.question: There ___ two banks on my street.

explanation.en: Use 'there are' to say that two or more things exist somewhere. In this meaning, Hebrew 'yesh' is 'there is/are', not 'have'.
explanation.he: כדי לומר שיש כמה דברים במקום מסוים משתמשים ב-there are. "יש" במשמעות הזאת הוא there is/are, ולא have.

items.question: My birthday is ___ May.

explanation.en: Use 'in' with months and years (in May), 'on' with days (on Monday) and 'at' with clock times (at six o'clock).
explanation.he: עם חודשים ושנים: in (in May). עם ימים: on. עם שעות: at.

items.question: My mother's brother is my ___.

explanation.en: Your mother's or father's brother is your uncle. A cousin is your uncle's or aunt's child.
explanation.he: האח של אמא או של אבא הוא uncle (דוד). cousin הוא בן דוד או בת דודה.

items.question: This phone costs a lot of money. It's very ___.

explanation.en: Something that costs a lot of money is expensive. The opposite is cheap.
explanation.he: משהו שעולה הרבה כסף הוא expensive (יקר). ההפך: cheap (זול).

items.question: I'm ___. Can I have some water, please?

explanation.en: When you want a drink, you are thirsty. When you want food, you are hungry.
explanation.he: כשרוצים לשתות אומרים I'm thirsty (צמא/ה). כשרוצים לאכול: I'm hungry (רעב/ה).

items.question: You can buy fresh bread at the ___.

explanation.en: A bakery makes and sells bread and cakes. A library is a place where you borrow books.
explanation.he: bakery היא מאפייה. library היא ספרייה, מקום שבו שואלים ספרים.

prompt.en: Read the message and answer the question.
prompt.he: קראו את ההודעה וענו על השאלה.

items.question:
Hi Sam, it's Dana. Sorry, I can't come to the beach today. I have an exam tomorrow and I need to study. Are you free on Saturday?

Why can't Dana go to the beach today?

explanation.en: Dana has an exam tomorrow and needs to study. She asks if Sam is free on Saturday, so she is not busy then.
explanation.he: דנה כותבת שיש לה מבחן מחר והיא צריכה ללמוד. היא גם שואלת אם סם פנוי בשבת, כלומר היא עצמה לא עסוקה אז.

prompt.en: Read the text and answer the question.
prompt.he: קראו את הטקסט וענו על השאלה.

items.question:
Omer is a nurse. He works at night, so he sleeps in the morning. He usually gets up at two o'clock and has lunch with his wife. Then he goes to the gym.

When does Omer sleep?

explanation.en: Omer works at night, so he sleeps in the morning and gets up at two o'clock.
explanation.he: עומר עובד בלילה, ולכן הוא ישן בבוקר וקם בשתיים בצהריים.

items.audio_text: The concert starts at a quarter past eight, so let's meet at eight o'clock outside the station.
items.question: What time will they meet?

explanation.en: They will meet at eight o'clock (8:00). The concert starts at a quarter past eight (8:15).
explanation.he: הם ייפגשו בשמונה (8:00). הקונצרט מתחיל בשמונה ורבע (8:15).

items.audio_text: Two coffees and an orange juice, please.
items.question: What does the customer order?
options: One coffee and two orange juices
Two teas and an orange juice
Two coffees and two orange juices
Two coffees and an orange juice

explanation.en: The customer asks for two coffees and an (one) orange juice.
explanation.he: ההזמנה היא שתי כוסות קפה וכוס מיץ תפוזים אחת (an orange juice).

items.question: Yesterday I ___ my keys at home, so I couldn't get into the office.

explanation.en: 'Leave' is irregular: leave – left – left. A finished action (yesterday) needs the past simple.
explanation.he: leave הוא פועל חריג: leave – left – left. על פעולה שהסתיימה (yesterday) משתמשים בעבר פשוט.

items.question: This phone is ___ than my old one.

explanation.en: Short adjectives add -er: cheap → cheaper. Don't use 'more' together with -er.
explanation.he: לשמות תואר קצרים מוסיפים er: cheap – cheaper. לא משלבים more עם er.

items.question: Please be quiet. The baby ___.

explanation.en: 'Please be quiet' shows the action is happening now, so we use the present continuous: is sleeping.
explanation.he: Please be quiet מראה שהפעולה קורית עכשיו, ולכן הווה מתמשך: is sleeping.

items.question: How ___ money do you need?

explanation.en: 'Money' is uncountable, so we ask 'How much?'. 'How many?' is for things you can count (How many coins?).
explanation.he: money הוא שם עצם שאינו ספיר, ולכן How much. את How many שואלים על דברים שאפשר לספור.

items.question: Can you ___ the music? It's too loud.

explanation.en: 'Turn down' means make quieter. 'Turn up' means make louder, and 'turn on' means start.
explanation.he: turn down = להנמיך. turn up = להגביר. turn on = להדליק.

items.question: Our flight was ___ by three hours because of the weather.

explanation.en: A delayed flight leaves later than planned. 'Missed' means you arrived too late for it.
explanation.he: delayed = התעכב, נדחה. missed = פספסנו את הטיסה (הגענו מאוחר מדי).

items.question: The museum tour was really ___. I almost fell asleep.

explanation.en: Use -ing for the thing that causes the feeling (the tour was boring) and -ed for how a person feels (I was bored).
explanation.he: הסיומת ing מתארת את מה שגורם לתחושה (the tour was boring), והסיומת ed את מה שהאדם מרגיש (I was bored).

items.question:
A: Let's go to the beach on Saturday.
B: ___ I love swimming.

explanation.en: 'That's a great idea!' accepts a suggestion. 'You're welcome' answers 'thank you', and 'Never mind' means 'it isn't important'.
explanation.he: That's a great idea! היא תשובה להצעה. את You're welcome אומרים בתגובה לתודה, ו-Never mind פירושו "לא חשוב".

prompt.en: Read the text and answer the question.
prompt.he: קראו את הטקסט וענו על השאלה.

items.question:
Last Saturday, Yael and her brother took the train to Haifa to visit their grandmother. The train was very crowded, so they stood for the whole trip. When they arrived, their grandmother was waiting for them at the station. In the evening, they all had dinner at a fish restaurant by the sea.

Why did Yael and her brother stand on the train?
options: They wanted to see the sea.

explanation.en: The train was very crowded (full of people), so there were no free seats.
explanation.he: הרכבת הייתה מלאה מאוד (crowded), ולכן לא היו מקומות פנויים לשבת.

prompt.en: Read the sign and answer the question.
prompt.he: קראו את השלט וענו על השאלה.

items.question:
Pool rules: Children under 12 must be with an adult at all times. Please shower before you go into the water. Food and glass bottles are not allowed in the pool area.

What do the rules ask all swimmers to do?

explanation.en: The rules say 'Please shower before you go into the water.' Only children under 12 need an adult, and food is not allowed.
explanation.he: בכללים כתוב להתקלח לפני שנכנסים למים. רק ילדים מתחת לגיל 12 צריכים מבוגר, ואוכל אסור באזור הבריכה.

items.audio_text: I can't meet on Tuesday because I'm visiting my grandparents. How about Wednesday afternoon?
items.question: When does the speaker want to meet?

explanation.en: The speaker is busy on Tuesday (visiting grandparents) and suggests Wednesday afternoon.
explanation.he: ביום שלישי יש ביקור אצל סבא וסבתא, ולכן ההצעה היא יום רביעי אחר הצהריים.

items.audio_text: We wanted to go to the beach yesterday, but it was too windy. So we stayed at home and played board games.
items.question: What did they do yesterday?

explanation.en: It was too windy for the beach, so they stayed at home and played board games.
explanation.he: הייתה רוח חזקה מדי, אז במקום ללכת לים הם נשארו בבית ושיחקו במשחקי קופסה.

items.question: I ___ in this city since 2020.

explanation.en: 'Since' + a starting point describes a situation that began in the past and continues now, so we need the present perfect: I have lived here since 2020. Hebrew uses the present here, which is why 'live' is tempting.
explanation.he: since עם נקודת התחלה מתאר מצב שהתחיל בעבר ונמשך עד היום, ולכן צריך present perfect: I have lived here since 2020. בעברית משתמשים כאן בהווה ("אני גר/ה כאן מאז 2020"), ולכן קל לטעות ולבחור ב-live.

items.question: If it ___ tomorrow, we'll stay at home.

explanation.en: In the first conditional the if-clause uses the present simple, even for the future: If it rains, we'll stay at home. Hebrew uses the future here, which is why 'will rain' is tempting.
explanation.he: במשפט תנאי מסוג ראשון, אחרי if משתמשים בהווה פשוט גם כשמדובר בעתיד: If it rains, we'll stay at home. בעברית אומרים כאן עתיד ("אם ירד גשם"), ולכן קל לבחור ב-will rain.

items.question: After a long conversation, she decided ___ the job offer.

explanation.en: 'Decide' is followed by to + infinitive: decide to accept. Verbs like 'enjoy' and 'avoid' take -ing instead.
explanation.he: אחרי decide באים to וצורת המקור של הפועל: decide to accept. אחרי פעלים כמו enjoy ו-avoid באה צורת ing.

items.question: This bridge ___ more than a hundred years ago.

explanation.en: The bridge didn't do the building, so we need the passive (was + past participle). 'Ago' points to a finished past time, so the past simple: was built.
explanation.he: הגשר לא בנה, אלא נבנה, ולכן צריך סביל (passive): was + צורת ה-past participle. ago מציין זמן שהסתיים בעבר, ולכן עבר פשוט: was built.

items.question: Can I ___ your charger? I left mine at home.

explanation.en: You borrow something from someone (you receive it); you lend something to someone (you give it). 'Can I lend your charger?' is a very common mistake.
explanation.he: borrow פירושו לשאול (לקבל משהו לזמן מה), ו-lend פירושו להשאיל (לתת). Can I lend your charger? היא טעות נפוצה מאוד.

items.question: Please ___ me to call the dentist tomorrow. I always forget.

explanation.en: 'Remind someone to do something' means help them remember. You remember something yourself; you can't 'remember someone to do' something.
explanation.he: remind someone to do something פירושו להזכיר למישהו לעשות משהו. remember פירושו לזכור בעצמך, ואי אפשר לומר remember someone to do something.

items.question: I'd love a new laptop, but I can't ___ one right now.

explanation.en: 'Afford' means to have enough money for something. 'Pay' needs 'for' (pay for one), and 'spend' and 'cost' don't fit this pattern.
explanation.he: afford פירושו שיש מספיק כסף למשהו (להרשות לעצמך). אחרי pay צריך for (pay for one), ו-spend ו-cost לא מתאימים למבנה הזה.

items.question: We've had to ___ the meeting until next week because the manager is away.

explanation.en: 'Put off' means postpone (move to a later time). You put out a fire, put on clothes and put away your things.
explanation.he: put off פירושו לדחות (להעביר למועד מאוחר יותר). put out = לכבות (למשל אש), put on = ללבוש, put away = להחזיר למקום.

prompt.en: Read the text and answer the question.
prompt.he: קראו את הטקסט וענו על השאלה.

items.question:
Many people think working from home is always easier. In my experience, it has clear advantages: I save two hours of travel every day, and I can concentrate better. However, I miss my colleagues, and it is sometimes hard to stop working in the evening. For me, two days a week at home is the right balance.

What is the writer's main point?
options: Working from home is easier than working in an office.
Working from home has both good and bad sides.
Most people are happier working in an office.
The main problem with working from home is working late.

explanation.en: The writer lists advantages (less travel, better concentration) and disadvantages (missing colleagues, working late) and prefers a balance. The first sentence is the view the writer questions, and working late is only one detail, not the main point.
explanation.he: הכותב מונה יתרונות (חיסכון בזמן נסיעה, ריכוז טוב יותר) וחסרונות (הגעגועים לעמיתים, הקושי להפסיק לעבוד בערב), ומעדיף איזון. המשפט הראשון מציג דעה שהכותב מטיל בה ספק, והעבודה עד שעה מאוחרת היא רק פרט אחד ולא הרעיון המרכזי.

prompt.en: Read the text and answer the question.
prompt.he: קראו את הטקסט וענו על השאלה.

items.question:
When Adi moved to Be'er Sheva for a new job, she didn't know anyone there. She joined a running club, and within a few weeks she had a group of close friends. That was two years ago. Today she says she can't imagine living anywhere else.

Which sentence about Adi is true today?
options: She is planning to move back.
She still doesn't know many people.
She is happy living in Be'er Sheva.
She has just started her job.

explanation.en: 'She can't imagine living anywhere else' shows she is happy there. She moved two years ago and made friends through the running club.
explanation.he: המשפט she can't imagine living anywhere else (היא לא מדמיינת את עצמה גרה במקום אחר) מראה שטוב לה שם. היא עברה לעיר לפני שנתיים והכירה חברים במועדון הריצה.

items.audio_text: Hi, this is Sarah from the dental clinic. Doctor Levi won't be in tomorrow, so we'd like to move your appointment to Thursday at the same time.
items.question: Why is Sarah calling?
options: To change the day of an appointment.
To move an appointment to later the same day.
To remind the listener about tomorrow's appointment.

explanation.en: The appointment moves from tomorrow to Thursday 'at the same time', so only the day changes, not the time.
explanation.he: התור עובר ממחר ליום חמישי at the same time (באותה שעה), כלומר רק היום משתנה, ולא השעה.

items.audio_text: Attention, please. The ten fifteen train to Jerusalem is running about twenty minutes late, and today it will not stop at the airport.
items.question: What are passengers told?
options: The train is late but will make all its usual stops.
The train will leave twenty minutes early.
The train will not run today.
The train is late and will skip one stop.

explanation.en: Two things change: the train is about twenty minutes late, and today it will not stop at the airport.
explanation.he: יש שני שינויים: הרכבת מאחרת בכעשרים דקות, והיום היא לא תעצור בשדה התעופה.

items.question: If I ___ about the traffic, I would have left earlier.

explanation.en: This is the third conditional (an unreal past): if + past perfect, would have + past participle. If I had known…, I would have left…

items.question: She was exhausted because she ___ all night.

explanation.en: The past perfect continuous describes an activity that went on up to a past moment and explains a result at that moment: she was exhausted because she had been studying.

items.question: He denied ___ the window, but nobody believed him.

explanation.en: 'Deny' is followed by -ing (denied breaking) or by a that-clause with its own subject (denied that he broke). 'Deny to do' is not possible.

items.question: The company is said ___ more than five hundred people.

explanation.en: The pattern is subject + is said + to-infinitive: The company is said to employ… The alternative is 'It is said that the company employs…'.

items.question: We worked all weekend to ___ the deadline.

explanation.en: 'Meet a deadline' is the standard collocation (the opposite is 'miss a deadline'). 'Reach', 'catch' and 'win' don't combine with 'deadline' in this sense.

items.question: Lior has been feeling under the ___ all week, so she's staying at home today.

explanation.en: 'Under the weather' is a fixed idiom meaning slightly ill. The other words don't form an idiom here.

items.question: You are emailing a university admissions office for the first time. Which request is the most appropriate?
options: I want you to send me the course details as soon as possible.
Can you send me the course info ASAP? Thanks a lot!
Send me the details of the course, please. I need them soon.
I would be grateful if you could send me the course details.

explanation.en: A first email to an institution calls for a polite, indirect request such as 'I would be grateful if you could…'. 'I want you to…' and a bare imperative ('Send me…') sound like demands in English, even when the Hebrew equivalents sound normal, and 'info', 'ASAP' and 'Thanks a lot!' are too casual for this reader.

items.question: The hotel was in a noisy area and quite far from the beach. ___, we really enjoyed our stay.

explanation.en: The second sentence contrasts with the first (problems, yet we enjoyed it), so we need a contrast connector: Nevertheless. 'Therefore' and 'consequently' introduce results, and 'moreover' adds a similar point.

prompt.en: Read the text and answer the question.

items.question:
Suppose an advertisement claims that 'nine out of ten dentists recommend' a particular toothpaste. What it does not say is how those dentists were chosen or what exactly they were asked. They may simply have agreed that the toothpaste was acceptable, not that it was better than any other.

What is the writer's main point?
options: The advertisement's claim may be misleading.

explanation.en: The writer points out missing information (how the dentists were chosen, what they were asked) to show that the claim may sound stronger than it is. Nothing is said about harm or about other toothpastes.

prompt.en: Read the text and answer the question.

items.question:
When the town council announced plans to turn the old post office into a hotel, few residents objected. It was only after photos of the building's original interior appeared online that a campaign to save it began. Within a month, the council had agreed to reconsider.

What does the text suggest?
options: Residents opposed the plan from the start.
The council refused to change its original plans.
The hotel has already been built.
The photos helped turn opinion against the plan.

explanation.en: Few residents objected at first, and a campaign began only after the photos appeared, so the photos helped turn opinion against the plan. The council agreed to reconsider, so it did not refuse, and nothing suggests the hotel has been built.

items.audio_text: To be honest, I expected a lot more from the sequel. The effects were impressive, but the plot was so predictable that I'd guessed the ending within twenty minutes.
items.question: What is the speaker's overall opinion of the sequel?

explanation.en: 'I expected a lot more' and the predictable plot show disappointment, even though the speaker praises the effects.

items.audio_text: I'd have been happy to help with the move, but nobody told me it was happening this weekend.
items.question: What does the speaker mean?
options: The speaker helped with the move last weekend.
The speaker was too busy to help.
The speaker didn't help because nobody told them.
The speaker has offered to help next weekend.

explanation.en: 'I'd have been happy to help' (would have + past participle) describes something that didn't happen: the speaker didn't help, because nobody said the move was this weekend.

items.question: Not only ___ late, but he also forgot the documents.

explanation.en: When a negative expression such as 'Not only' starts the clause, the subject and auxiliary are inverted: Not only did he arrive late…

items.question: ___ you require any further information, please do not hesitate to contact us.

explanation.en: 'Should you require…' is a formal inverted conditional meaning 'If you require…'. 'Would' cannot open a conditional clause like this, 'Had you require' is ungrammatical, and 'Unless' reverses the meaning.

items.question: ___ the report twice, she sent it to her manager.

explanation.en: A perfect participle clause (having + past participle) shows that one action was completed before the next, with the same subject: she checked the report, then sent it. 'Having been checked' is passive, so it cannot take an object ('the report') and would make 'she' the thing that was checked.

items.question: It was only when I moved abroad ___ I understood how much my parents had done for me.

explanation.en: In an it-cleft, the part in focus is followed by 'that': It was only when I moved abroad that I understood… Repeating 'when' is a common error.

items.question: There has been a marked ___ in public trust since the scandal.

explanation.en: 'A marked decline' is a standard academic collocation. 'Declination' and 'declension' are technical terms with different meanings, and 'declining' cannot follow 'a marked' here.

items.question: Imagine a small survey found that students who slept less tended to get lower exam results. Which conclusion is worded most appropriately for an academic essay?
options: This demonstrates that a lack of sleep causes poor exam results.
The survey suggests a possible link between sleep and exam results.
It is certain that every student should sleep more before exams.
This shows clearly that sleep has no real effect on exam results.

explanation.en: A small survey can show a link but cannot prove a cause. 'Suggests a possible link' matches the strength of the evidence; 'demonstrates… causes' and 'it is certain' overstate it, and 'no real effect' contradicts the finding.

items.question: The study's conclusions are ___ by its very small sample.

explanation.en: 'Undermine' means weaken: a tiny sample weakens the conclusions. 'Underline' means highlight, 'undertake' means carry out, and 'understate' means present something as smaller than it is.

items.question: Her argument was ___: every point was backed up by clear evidence.

explanation.en: 'Compelling' means convincing. 'Compulsory' means required, 'compulsive' describes something a person can't stop doing, and 'complacent' means too satisfied to see problems.

prompt.en: Read the text and answer the question.

items.question:
The author of the report is careful to acknowledge that her survey relied on volunteers, who may care more about the issue than most people do. Even so, she goes on to draw sweeping conclusions about 'all young people', as though this limitation had never been raised.

What criticism does the writer make of the report's author?
options: She failed to mention that her survey used volunteers.
Her conclusions go further than her own evidence allows.
She did not explain how the survey was carried out.
She relied too heavily on expert opinion.

explanation.en: She admits the sample may be unrepresentative but still makes claims about 'all young people'. The writer says she did mention the volunteers ('careful to acknowledge'), so that option is wrong.

prompt.en: Read the text and answer the question.

items.question:
The novel's first hundred pages are a pleasure: sharp, funny and beautifully observed. It is a pity, then, that the author seems to lose interest in her characters halfway through, leaving the final chapters to be carried by a plot that grows ever more far-fetched.

Which option best sums up the reviewer's view?
options: The novel starts strongly but becomes less convincing.
The novel is excellent from beginning to end.
The characters become more interesting in the final chapters.
The plot is the strongest part of the novel.

explanation.en: Praise for the opening ('a pleasure') is followed by criticism: the author 'loses interest' in the characters, and the plot becomes 'far-fetched' (hard to believe).

items.audio_text: To be fair, the proposal isn't without its merits, but I'd want to see a far more detailed budget before I'd be prepared to put my name to it.
items.question: What is the speaker's position on the proposal?
options: Supports it fully and is ready to sign it.
Rejects it outright because of its cost.
Sees some value in it but won't back it yet.
Has signed it but wants a more detailed budget.

explanation.en: 'Isn't without its merits' means it has some good points; 'before I'd be prepared to put my name to it' shows the speaker won't back it until there is a detailed budget. So the speaker has neither signed nor rejected it: the problem is the missing detail in the budget, not the cost.

items.audio_text: Had the warning been taken seriously when it was first issued, much of the damage could have been avoided.
items.question: What does the speaker imply?
options: The warning was taken seriously, so the damage was limited.
There was no warning before the damage.
The damage could not have been prevented.
The warning was not taken seriously at first.

explanation.en: 'Had the warning been taken seriously' is an inverted third conditional (= If the warning had been taken seriously). It implies that it was not, and that much of the damage was avoidable.

items.question: Such ___ the demand for tickets that the website crashed within minutes.

explanation.en: In 'Such + be + subject + that…', the verb agrees with the subject that follows it, 'the demand' (singular): Such was the demand that… 'Tickets' is not the subject.

items.question: Much ___ I admire her work, I can't agree with her conclusions.

explanation.en: 'Much as' is a concessive meaning 'although… very much': Much as I admire her work = Although I admire her work very much. The other words don't form this structure.

items.question: The minister, ___ to have known about the problem for months, has so far refused to comment.

explanation.en: This is a reduced passive clause: The minister, (who is) believed to have known… Active forms such as 'believing' or 'who believed' would make the minister the one doing the believing.

items.question: Were the government ___ this policy, it would face fierce opposition.

explanation.en: 'Were + subject + to-infinitive' is a formal inverted conditional: Were the government to introduce… = If the government were to introduce…

items.question: She's careful with money. Some would unkindly call her ___, but I'd say she's simply sensible.

explanation.en: 'Unkindly' and the contrast with 'simply sensible' require a word with a negative connotation. 'Miserly' suggests meanness; 'thrifty', 'frugal' and 'economical' are neutral or positive.

items.question: The annual report makes for ___ reading: almost every target has been missed.

explanation.en: 'Make for sobering reading' is a fixed collocation: the text is serious and makes you think. 'Sobered' describes a person's reaction, 'solemn' doesn't collocate here, and 'soothing' has the opposite effect.

items.question: The review damned the album with ___ praise, calling it 'perfectly competent'.

explanation.en: 'Damn with faint praise' means praising something so mildly that the praise sounds like criticism, and 'perfectly competent' is exactly that kind of praise. The idiom is fixed: only 'faint' is used.

items.question: The two accounts of the meeting are hard to ___: one describes a unanimous decision, the other a bitter split.

explanation.en: To 'reconcile' two accounts is to show how both can be true together. 'Rectify' means correct, 'retract' means withdraw a statement, and 'reclaim' means get something back.

prompt.en: Read the text and answer the question.

items.question:
The council's new 'efficiency plan' has been a triumph. In just six months it has managed to double the time it takes to renew a parking permit. The consultants who designed it, meanwhile, have been rewarded with a second contract.

What does the writer imply about the consultants?
options: They fully deserved the second contract.
They designed the plan in six months.
They were rewarded despite the plan's failure.
They were not paid for their first contract.

explanation.en: 'A triumph' is ironic: doubling the waiting time is a failure. 'Meanwhile… rewarded' draws attention to the gap between the result and the consultants' reward.

prompt.en: Read the text and answer the question.

items.question:
Early studies of the teaching method reported dramatic gains. Later work, using larger samples and stricter controls, found effects that were real but modest. The most defensible position, then, is neither the enthusiasts' nor the critics'.

What is the writer's conclusion about the method?
options: It works, but less dramatically than first claimed.
It does not work, despite the early reports.
The early studies were more reliable than the later ones.
No conclusion can be drawn from the research.

explanation.en: The writer weighs both sets of studies and concludes the effect is 'real but modest'. That rejects both the enthusiasts' 'dramatic gains' and the critics' view that the method does not work.

items.audio_text: I'm sure the committee had its reasons. I'd just be fascinated to hear what they were.
items.question: What does the speaker imply?
options: The speaker agrees with the committee's decision.
The speaker doubts that the committee had good reasons.
The speaker already knows the committee's reasons.
The speaker would like to join the committee.

explanation.en: 'I'm sure the committee had its reasons' followed by 'I'd just be fascinated to hear what they were' is polite irony: the speaker suggests the reasons are hard to find.

items.audio_text: Far be it from me to tell you how to run your department, but I'd have thought the deadline was the one thing you couldn't afford to miss.
items.question: What is the speaker doing?
options: Praising the way the listener runs the department.
Offering to help the listener meet the deadline.
Indirectly finding fault with the listener.

explanation.en: 'Far be it from me to…' introduces exactly what the speaker claims not to do. The speaker points out the listener's mistake while appearing not to interfere.
